verdict.rationale: Gazebo can run headless (server-only) and be fully controlled/introspected via gz-transport (TCP/IP pub-sub) and extensive CLI tools, meaning most simulation state and control available in the GUI can also be accessed programmatically. However, there's no evidence of a unified REST/OpenAPI-style API parity layer — the GUI is plugin-based and some interactions (visual introspection, model browsing via Fuel UI) aren't shown to have a documented 1:1 programmatic equivalent, and probes for llms.txt/openapi.json all 404. missing for 10: documented API-to-UI feature parity mapping, official OpenAPI/REST spec, evidence that GUI-only features (e.g. Fuel browsing, visual plugin config) have full programmatic equivalents.
